$comment: Places where an official schema and its own official documentation disagree, or where a stated rule cannot be expressed in the schema that is supposed to enforce it. Each entry records both positions, what the official sample file actually does, and which one a filer should follow. These are the failures that pass XSD validation and are rejected by the portal — or the reverse.

documentationSays.quote: must be either "Y" for Yes or "N" for No

conflicts.resolution: Send true or false. Y and N are not valid xs:boolean lexical values and would fail schema validation.
conflicts.impact: A generator written from the annotation produces a file that fails validation on every employee row.

schemaSays.declaration: xs:string with minLength 1 and maxLength 50 — no pattern

documentationSays.quote: must be two uppercase letters of the state abbreviation. For example: CA

guideSays.summary: Invalid state abbreviations are listed among the upload errors; full names are required.

conflicts.resolution: Send the full state name. The two-letter abbreviation the annotation asks for is what the portal rejects.
conflicts.impact: Schema-valid either way. The abbreviation fails at upload, after the file has already passed local XSD validation.

schemaSays.declaration: both declared minOccurs="0" and independent — neither, either or both validate

guideSays.quote: a value in either dateOfBirth or ssnLast4; you cannot include a value in both

conflicts.resolution: Supply exactly one. An xs:choice would have expressed this; the schema does not use one.
conflicts.impact: The most common schema-valid, portal-invalid file. Nothing local catches it unless you check for it yourself.

schemaSays.declaration: no minOccurs attribute, so it defaults to 1 — required

guideSays.summary: lists country among the optional elements

conflicts.resolution: Send it. Omitting it fails schema validation regardless of what the guide says.
conflicts.impact: Omission fails at step 1 of validation.

documentationSays.quote: must match name id attribute SSN of "SSN::NAME"

schemaSays.declaration: version 2.0 has no name element and no id attribute anywhere; names are firstName, middleName and lastName

conflicts.resolution: Ignore the sentence. It describes a structure that does not exist in this format — though it is precisely the convention California's schema does use.
conflicts.impact: None on validity. It sends implementers looking for a field that is not there.

schemaSays.declaration: a day element whose first child is also named day and holds the xs:date

conflicts.resolution: Legal XML, and the official sample does exactly this. Note it before writing XPath or generating bindings.
conflicts.impact: Naive code-generation and XPath expressions silently address the wrong node.

schemaSays.declaration: xs:string restricted to ([0-9]{1,4})(\.[0-9]{1,2})? — no more than four digits before the decimal point

conflicts.resolution: No single deduction may be 10000.00 or more, and the value carries no sign. Split or aggregate accordingly.
conflicts.impact: A large garnishment or benefit deduction fails validation with a pattern error that does not say why.
conflicts.note: The sibling deductionsGrossEarnings and netWages are xs:decimal up to 999999.99, so the tighter cap applies only to individual deduction lines.

schemaSays.declaration: default minOccurs of 1 with minLength 0 — the element must be present, its content may be empty

guideSays.quote: isn't mandatory and can be left blank

conflicts.resolution: Send the element with empty content. "Not mandatory" refers to the content, not to the element.
conflicts.impact: Omitting the element fails schema validation.

guideSays.quote: All other fields must be empty

schemaSays.quote: If you do not have this number, please enter valid awardingBodyId, projectNum, and contractID so the system can properly look up the registered PWC-100 public project

conflicts.resolution: The three elements are not declared fixed="" — unlike awardingBody, contractAgencyID, projectName and every child of projectLocation, which are — so the schema permits the lookup path the annotation describes. Prefer a real projectID; fall back to the lookup triple only if you have no projectID.
conflicts.impact: Following the guide literally removes the only documented fallback for a filer who does not know the project ID.

guideSays.summary: the guideline states no per-file limit

conflicts.resolution: Split at 500 employees per file — the same cap New York applies to employee work weeks, arrived at independently.
conflicts.impact: A large contractor's weekly file fails validation with no documented explanation.

documentationSays.summary: the guideline PDF is titled Version 1.10, dated January 2016, and its release notes section is headed 1.5

conflicts.resolution: There is no single version number for the California format. Pin to the schema's own comment and record the date you retrieved it.
conflicts.impact: Version pinning and change detection have to be done by content hash, not by a published version.

schemaSays.declaration: ssn is required and restricted to [0-9]{9}; numWithholdingExemp is required and restricted to [0-9]{1,2}

federalSays.summary: WH-347 column 1E takes the last four digits or a worker-specific number, and full Social Security numbers must not be included; the January 2025 revision removed the withholding-exemptions column entirely

conflicts.resolution: Neither is wrong. The same worker record carries a full SSN in the California file and must not carry one in the federal form, and California still collects a field the federal form no longer has. Derive each output from a canonical record; do not reuse one file as the other.
conflicts.impact: The single clearest reason a certified payroll file cannot be reused across jurisdictions.

conflicts.element: amendedFlag, amendedDate, amendReason, WageID, apprenticePgmOccpnID, apprenticePgmName, apprenticePgmOccpnStepCalcID

schemaSays.declaration: the elements are still declared in the PWIA schema

guideSays.summary: they can be removed from the file, and if included must be null; L&I states it is working on removing them from the schema

conflicts.resolution: Omit them. If your generator emits them, emit them null.
conflicts.impact: A file generated straight from the schema carries seven fields the system does not want populated.
